validity.researcher_notes: The sheet length 365 km and diameter 800 mm match KGMO-1, which was commissioned in 1963. The 90 billion cubic meter figure comes from the decree item for the KGMO-2 reconstruction.

fills.researcher_notes: Item 38 of the federal planning decree gives 90 billion cubic meters a year as the design volume for the reconstruction of KGMO-2 between Noginsk and Voskresensk, described as raising the capacity of the Moscow Region ring. It is a planned figure and it sits on the KGMO-2 item, so the tier is low.
A Gazprom Transgaz Moscow news item of June 2018, Wayback capture, gives KGMO-1 as 365.5 km. The sheet has 365 km, so it agrees within rounding.

fills.researcher_notes: The same letter, signed by a unit of Gazprom Transgaz Moscow, says KGMO-1 is run by that company.

The letter and the 2018 news item name Gazprom Transgaz Moscow as the operator and say it is a wholly owned subsidiary of Gazprom. Neither says who holds the pipeline, so the owner on the sheet was not confirmed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The Transgaz Moscow letter says KGMO-1 is in operation and registered as a hazardous production facility. The 2018 news item gives its length as 365.5 km.

wiki_citations_read.note: The scheme describes the two-string Moscow Region ring (KGMO-1 and KGMO-2), three compressor stations, and planned reconstruction of KGMO-1 sections to a 1200 mm nominal diameter. It says the trunk objects in the new Moscow territories belong to Gazprom PJSC and are operated by Gazprom Transgaz Moscow LLC, built between 1961 and 1985, but does not name the ring in that sentence. It states no 365 km length, 800 mm diameter or 90 bcm/y capacity. Owner stays unresolved.
